name: Holy Hill National Shrine of Mary, Help of Christians
architect: Hermann J. Gaul and Richard Philipp
history: By tradition, Father Jacques Marquette passed this hill in 1673, though historians doubt it. Irish settlers called it Holy Hill, and a log chapel to Mary, Help of Christians, was dedicated in 1863. Discalced Carmelites from Bavaria took charge in 1906. The present church's cornerstone was laid in 1926 and it was consecrated in 1931. It became a basilica in 2006.
arch: A Romanesque Revival church with twin spires on a high glacial hill (a kame) in 400 acres of woods.
features: A 178-step observation tower looks out to the Milwaukee skyline, about thirty miles away.

look.d: The spires can be seen for miles across the Kettle Moraine.
Carmelite friars have cared for the shrine since 1906.

fun: The hill's first known resident was a hermit named François Soubrio.
journal: Spires above autumn woods. Climb 178 steps and Milwaukee floats on the horizon.
